transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My mind just won't shut off about work and everything else, and I can't seem to turn the worrying off no matter what I do. It has gotten to the point where I feel completely overwhelmed, so a friend suggested I finally come in to talk to someone.
Can you tell me if you've experienced any panic attacks, where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, or if your worrying is more of a constant, ongoing state?

I don't really experience those sudden, peak-and-fade panic attacks; it's definitely more of a constant, ongoing state of worry. My mind is always running worst-case scenarios like a YouTube autoplay I can't pause, and I just feel wired and on edge almost all the time.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain situations, places, or activities because of your worries or fears?

Yes, I have. I've started canceling plans with my friends and skipping my usual dance nights and hikes. I just feel too anxious, exhausted, and completely drained by the constant worrying to keep up with them anymore.
Have you experienced any traumatic events in your past that might be contributing to your current state of anxiety and worry?
No, I haven't experienced any traumatic events in my past that I can think of. My anxiety seems to be mostly tied to my recent work promotion and all the new responsibilities that came with it.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like tremors, sweating, or difficulty sleeping that accompany your feelings of anxiety and worry?

I don't really have tremors or sweating, but my sleep is terrible—I'm often awake until 2 a.m. replaying work emails and wake up feeling completely unrefreshed. I also feel constantly wired and physically tense, like I'm always clenching my shoulders and tapping my foot.

Can you tell me if your excessive worry is focused primarily on one specific aspect of your life, such as work, or if it's more generalized and encompasses multiple areas, like work, finances, relationships, and daily life?

It's definitely not just about work, though that is a huge trigger for me. Once the worry starts, it quickly spirals into everything else, like my student loans, my parents' health, and this constant fear that I'm going to lose my apartment or disappoint my family. It feels like my mind is always finding some new disaster to focus on.
Can you estimate how many different areas of your life you regularly worry about, and are there any specific themes that your worries tend to revolve around most frequently?

I'd say I worry about almost every area of my life, and it feels completely overwhelming. The main themes are work, like messing up automation scripts, failing the people I mentor, or getting fired, but I also constantly stress about my parents' health, disappointing my family, and financial things like student loans and losing my apartment. It just feels like there's always some disaster waiting to happen.
Can you describe how often you feel restless or on edge, and does it seem to be triggered by specific situations or is it a more constant feeling for you?

It's a constant feeling for me, and I feel wired and on edge most of the time rather than just in specific situations. It honestly feels like I've had way too much coffee even when I haven't, to the point where I'm always clenching my shoulders and tapping my foot. I can't seem to just sit and breathe without feeling like something is about to go wrong.

Have you noticed any changes in your interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like your dance nights and hikes, or has your anxiety primarily affected your ability to participate in them due to worry rather than a loss of interest?

I definitely haven't lost interest in them, and I actually really miss the balance they used to give me. I've just been skipping them because I feel completely exhausted, anxious, and overwhelmed by trying to keep up with my heavy work queue and other commitments.

Can you tell me if there are any specific thoughts or beliefs about yourself that you worry about, such as being a failure or not meeting expectations, or if your worries are more focused on external events and circumstances?

It’s really a mix of both. I worry deeply about failing and not meeting expectations, like making a mistake on a script or saying something stupid while mentoring and disappointing everyone. At the same time, my mind also gets completely overwhelmed by external things I can't control, like my student loans and my parents' health.

Can you tell me if you have experienced any periods in the past six months where you felt completely free from these worries and anxiety for at least a couple of days, or has it been a persistent issue?

No, it has been completely persistent without any breaks at all. For the entire nine months since my promotion, there hasn't been a single day where the worry and tension went away, not even on weekends when I'm trying to relax. It has just been a constant weight.

You mentioned your worries span multiple areas of your life, including work, finances, relationships, and daily life. Can you clarify if there's a predominant theme or area that your worries most frequently return to, or do they seem to shift fairly evenly across these different domains?

Work is definitely the most frequent starting point or trigger, but the worries don't stay there. Once they start, they quickly cascade and shift to other things like my student loans, my parents' health, and disappointing my family. It really feels like a chain reaction where the focus is constantly moving rather than staying on just one thing.
You mentioned feeling physically tense, like you're always clenching your shoulders and tapping your foot. How often would you say you experience this muscle tension, is it present most of the day?

Yes, it is pretty much constant and present throughout most of the day. I feel so wired and on edge, almost like I've had way too much coffee, and I find myself clenching my shoulders and tapping my foot from morning until night. It makes it incredibly difficult to just sit, breathe, and actually relax.
Can you describe if your excessive worry is typically accompanied by feelings of fear, or is it more about the anticipation of potential problems or making mistakes?

It is definitely more about anticipating potential problems and making mistakes rather than a sudden feeling of fear. My mind is constantly running worst-case scenarios, like worrying that I'll mess up a coding script for my big client, say something stupid while mentoring, or cause some disaster that gets me fired. It just feels like I'm always trying to prevent a catastrophe before it happens.
Can you describe a recent situation where you felt your worry or anxiety was disproportionate to the actual threat or danger, and how you responded to it?

Just last week, a minor task like writing an automation script triggered this massive spiral where I convinced myself I'd mess it up, get fired, lose my apartment, and disappoint my family. I responded by staying up all night triple-checking the configuration and running through hypothetical failures, which left me completely exhausted. I even ended up canceling my dance night just to keep obsessing over it, even though the script was actually fine.
